analysis.title: GS TWIG Notes: This Week in Global Research - October 30, 2026
key_insights: Goldman's baseline global growth forecast for 2027 matches 2026's pace and its potential growth estimate. Jan Hatzius sees downside risks building from higher-for-longer energy prices and rates, a fading AI expansion impulse, and potential AI labor disruption. GS expects fewer rate hikes than are currently priced in.
Current growth data is more encouraging. US 3Q GDP came in above expectations on consumer spending, core PCE was in line, and GS launched Q4 GDP tracking at +1.8%.
Euro area elections next year in France, Italy and Spain could push fiscal spending higher (Fillipo Taddei).
Taiwan: Goohoon Kwon raised GDP growth forecasts by 30-40bp for 2026 and 2027, citing the fastest corporate loan growth in almost 30 years, and expects a rate hike cycle to begin in December.
Emerging markets: the energy shock has had a muted impact on growth across most countries (Kevin Daly, Ludovica Ambrosino).

China investment growth slowed to 1.9% in 3Q26. Yuting Wang now expects property to fall to 8% of real GDP by 2030 from a 30% peak, a deeper downturn than previously anticipated, though the growth drag should ease gradually.

AI labor impact is broadening beyond Tech jobs. Displaced workers are taking longer to find new jobs, and those jobs are often as exposed to AI as the old ones (Pierfrancesco Mei). In China, high-tech and AI-related industries are likely to create fewer jobs than the property and services sectors lose (Chelsea Song).

The Fed and ECB held rates. GS economists keep forecasts for one more hike from each bank in December and none after. A third hike in March is possible if inflation runs higher than expected, for example from higher-for-longer oil prices.
The BoJ held rates and now forecasts higher fuel-driven inflation in 2027. The BoC hiked 25bp, as expected, with a hawkish tone on inflation and a raised growth forecast.
Vickie Chang reviews how macro assets traded in past Fed hiking cycles. Amanda Lynam is neutral on AI credit, underweight CCCs, and prefers single-Bs over BBs.

Coffee: Lina Thomas forecasts prices to keep declining as strong planting yields are realized. The bumper crop may be short lived, and the narrow breadth of ICE's coffee futures market may keep front-month prices highly volatile.

Brazil after Lula's re-election: upstream oil and gas producers (PRIO, PBR) remain structurally advantaged over downstream distributors (Vibra, Ultrapar) under current policies. Utilities (Axia, Sabesp, Equatorial) and infrastructure (WEG) offer high real yields with operational divergence. WEG was upgraded to Buy.
Irma Sgarz favors Brazilian retailers with structural (MELI), defensive (Raia Drogasil) or resilient (Smartfit) growth.

Chinese shipbuilders keep their dominant global position on container and bulker demand, offsetting slightly softer tanker demand. Industrial automation growth is led by semis, autos, electronics and lithium batteries, and domestic China makers ceded share in 3Q26.

European luxury shows rising divergence across brands, categories, consumers and regions. In China jewelry, GS favors Chow Tai Fook and Laopu for defensive earnings or structural growth amid gold volatility.

Semis materials: rising investment in 2027-30 capacity implies a fiercer future semi supply shortage, supporting pricing and profitability for materials makers (Chao Wang). A TrendForce expert session supports a positive 2027 DRAM/HBM pricing outlook, with meaningful DRAM capacity hard to add before 2028.

ESMO highlights: targeted therapies and bi-specific antibodies are replacing conventional chemotherapy, with growing focus on tolerability and combination synergies. Otsuka, VERA and VRTX presented positive Ph3 data in IgA nephropathy.

AI and cloud demand is outpacing physical infrastructure capacity, creating backlogs that weigh on revenue and push capex higher (AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT reviews). Hyperscaler capex is on pace for another record in 2027, but the amount they need to borrow is less than many fear.
SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics say they are sold out through 2028-2029. INTC said CPU demand could reach a $200bn TAM by 2030.
Copper: declining grades, rising capital intensity, permitting complexity and geopolitical fragmentation make the next wave of supply harder to deliver, per GS's Global Metals & Mining Conference.
Three ideas: Sumitomo Bakelite (initiate at Buy), GTT (upgrade to Buy, LNG containment leader), and Synspective (initiate at Buy, Japanese SAR satellite operator).

market_movers.rationale: Atsushi Ikeda cites AI server adoption, rising heat generation, advanced packaging and LEO satellite communications as drivers of profit growth at the Japanese chemicals company Sumitomo Bakelite.
Michele Della Vigna sees GTT, the LNG containment systems leader, benefiting from the LNG shipping cycle given its competitive moat, asset-light licensing model, and exposure at Asian shipyards.
Yuichiro Isayama sees Synspective, a pure-play Japanese satellite operator, benefiting from growing SAR technology demand and government investment given its edge in constellation geometry.
GS upgraded WEG SA to Buy as part of its Brazil infrastructure and utilities coverage.
A podcast listing references GS's upgrade of CoreWeave to Buy, discussed by Gabriela Borges.

sector_views.rationale: Neutral on AI credit, underweight CCCs, preferring single-Bs over BBs.
Upstream producers (PRIO, PBR) are structurally advantaged over downstream distributors (Vibra, Ultrapar) under current policies.
Utilities and infrastructure offer high real yields, with clear operational divergence among names.
Rising investment in future capacity implies a fiercer semi supply shortage, supporting pricing and profitability for materials makers.
2027 DRAM/HBM pricing outlook is positive and meaningful DRAM capacity is difficult to add before 2028.
Favors jewelers with defensive earnings or structural growth drivers, robust ROE and overseas white space: Chow Tai Fook and Laopu.

earnings_insights: AMZN Q3'26, GOOGL Q3'26 and MSFT 1QFY reviews: AI and cloud demand is outpacing physical infrastructure capacity, creating backlogs that weigh on revenue and drive capex higher. No figures are given in this note.
SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics earnings reviews: both say they are sold out through 2028-2029.
INTC reported strong server demand and highlighted that CPU demand could reach a $200bn TAM by 2030 (a company projection, not a reported result).
European luxury 3Q26 wrap: divergence across brands, categories, consumer types and regions. No figures are given in this note.

macro_indicators.reading: Higher than expected, driven by consumer spending
macro_indicators.interpretation: Current growth is holding up despite GS's view that downside risks are building.
No upside inflation surprise from this print.

macro_indicators.reading: Held; GS forecasts one more hike in December
macro_indicators.interpretation: A measured approach remains appropriate, with no hikes after December in the baseline.

risk_factors: Higher-for-longer energy prices and rates weigh on the global growth trajectory.
A fading AI expansion impulse could slow growth.
AI-driven labor disruption is broadening beyond Tech jobs.
A deeper China property downturn and slowing investment.
Higher-for-longer oil prices could push inflation above GS forecasts and bring a third Fed and ECB hike in March.
The AI infrastructure bottleneck is unlikely to ease soon, with backlogs weighing on cloud revenue.
Copper supply constraints from declining grades, capital intensity and permitting.
Narrow breadth in ICE coffee futures may keep front-month prices highly volatile.
geopolitical: Brazil: Lula's re-election this week and the resulting policy outlook for fuels pricing, diesel subsidies (extended one month), export taxes and M&A.
Energy shock with higher-for-longer oil prices affecting growth, inflation and balance of payments in emerging markets.
Geopolitical fragmentation is making copper supply harder to deliver, and governments are increasingly focused on resource security.
US midterm elections, with GS webinars on November 4 covering the first take and post-mortem.
Euro area elections next year in France, Italy and Spain may push fiscal spending higher.
UK Budget covered in GS podcasts.

tension_points.bull_case: Current growth news is encouraging: US 3Q GDP beat on consumer spending, Taiwan forecasts were raised, and EM growth has been little hurt by the energy shock.
tension_points.bear_case: Hatzius sees downside risks building from higher-for-longer energy prices and rates, a fading AI expansion impulse and potential AI labor disruption, plus China investment slowing to 1.9%.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler capex is on pace for another record in 2027, but the amount they need to borrow is less than many fear.
tension_points.bear_case: The infrastructure bottleneck is unlikely to go away soon, creating backlogs that weigh on revenue.
